summary: H.R. 10761, the Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026, amends the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act and other federal statutes to address campus sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence, sexual harassment, and stalking. It introduces new reporting and transparency requirements for institutions of higher education, mandates the designation of confidential campus specialists for support services, establishes standardized disciplinary procedures and training guidelines, and authorizes financial penalties for noncompliance.

affected_groups.effect: Must update annual security reports, publish detailed safety data online, establish confidential specialist positions, adopt uniform disciplinary processes, train employees, and face potential civil penalties of up to one percent of their operating budget for noncompliance.

Receive new procedural rights, written notices of disciplinary decisions, access to confidential specialists, potential institutional amnesty for certain drug or alcohol violations, and clear protections against retaliation when reporting misconduct.

Must maintain a centralized public campus safety website, provide technical assistance, establish regulations through negotiated rulemaking, collect annual contact and training documentation for Title IX coordinators and specialists, and oversee civil penalty enforcement.
affected_groups.group: Department of Education and Department of Justice

key_provisions: Requires eligible institutions to include detailed statistical data regarding specific crimes—such as rape, fondling, incest, and statutory rape—and their handling through Title IX and student disciplinary processes in annual security reports.

Mandates the creation of a publicly available, searchable Department of Education website featuring compliance reviews, investigations, resolution agreements, and institutional data related to campus safety and Title IX.

Requires institutions of higher education to designate confidential sexual and interpersonal violence specialists who can assist victims, provide trauma-informed information, arrange accommodations, and report anonymized statistics without triggering mandatory investigations.

Establishes uniform campus-wide student disciplinary processes for handling claims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, sexual harassment, and stalking, prohibiting different procedures based on a student's status or athletic membership.
Authorizes the Secretary of Education to impose civil penalties of up to 1 percent of an institution's operating budget for each year the institution fails to meet the specified requirements.
Expands existing grant programs under the Violence Against Women and Department of Justice Reauthorization Act of 2005 to explicitly include sexual harassment.
Directs the Comptroller General to conduct a study and submit a report within two years on the effectiveness and efficiency of campus safety grant programs.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for institutional operating budgets when calculating penalties
Specific staffing ratios or numbers for what constitutes an adequate number of sexual and interpersonal violence specialists based on institution size, which are left to future negotiated rulemaking
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10761, the Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026, amends the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act and other federal statutes to address campus sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence, sexual harassment, and stalking. It introduces new reporting and transparency requirements for institutions of higher education, mandates the designation of confidential campus specialists for support services, establishes standardized disciplinary procedures and training guidelines, and authorizes financial penalties for noncompliance.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal oversight of campus safety by imposing strict reporting mandates, standardized disciplinary rules, and financial penalties on colleges and universities receiving federal funds, while expanding federal tracking and support structures for victims of sexual misconduct.
